fields.description: Issue dated June 2, 1928, featuring extensive coverage and commentary on the closing days of the Florida/Dade County Democratic primary campaign. Editorials criticize perceived bias and misinformation in Miami’s daily newspapers regarding statewide races (including Doyle Carlton, John Martin, and Fons Hathaway) and report on political rallies and heckling. The issue includes explanations of second-choice voting, numerous paid political advertisements (notably the Dade County sheriff’s race involving M. P. “Pop” Lehman, Henry R. Chase, and Louis Allen), local news items, a feature on a juvenile movie contest at Roney Plaza pools, discussion of greyhound coursing as cruelty to animals, and civic commentary on high school costs, local manufacturing, and Miami’s airport.
